pairs: Responsio mollis frangit iram;
A mild response shatters anger.
sermo durus suscitat furorem.
But a harsh word stirs up fury.
Lingua sapientium ornat scientiam;
The tongue of the wise adorns knowledge.
os fatuorum ebullit stultitiam.
But the mouth of the senseless gushes with foolishness.
In omni loco,
In every place,
oculi Domini contemplantur bonos et malos.
the eyes of the Lord consider good and evil.
Lingua placabilis lignum vitæ;
A peaceful tongue is a tree of life.
quæ autem immoderata est conteret spiritum.
But that which is immoderate will crush the spirit.
Stultus irridet disciplinam patris sui;
A fool laughs at the discipline of his father.
qui autem custodit increpationes astutior fiet.
But whoever preserves rebukes will become astute.
In abundanti justitia virtus maxima est:
In abundant justice, there is very great virtue.
cogitationes autem impiorum eradicabuntur.
But the intentions of the impious will be eradicated.
Domus justi plurima fortitudo,
The house of the just has very great strength.
et in fructibus impii conturbatio.
And in the fruits of the impious, there is disorder.
Labia sapientium disseminabunt scientiam;
The lips of the wise shall disseminate knowledge.
cor stultorum dissimile erit.
The heart of the foolish will be dissimilar.
Victimæ impiorum abominabiles Domino;
The sacrifices of the impious are abominable to the Lord.
vota justorum placabilia.
The vows of the just are appeasing.
Abominatio est Domino via impii;
The way of the impious is an abomination to the Lord.
qui sequitur justitiam diligitur ab eo.
Whoever pursues justice is loved by him.
Doctrina mala deserenti viam vitæ;
Doctrine is evil to those who abandon the way of life.
qui increpationes odit, morietur.
Whoever hates correction shall die.
Infernus et perditio coram Domino;
Hell and perdition are in the sight of the Lord.
quanto magis corda filiorum hominum!
How much more the hearts of the sons of men!
Non amat pestilens eum qui se corripit,
He who corrupts himself does not love the one who afflicts him,
nec ad sapientes graditur.
nor will he step toward the wise.
Cor gaudens exhilarat faciem;
A rejoicing heart gladdens the face.
in mœrore animi dejicitur spiritus.
But by the grief of the soul, the spirit is cast down.
Cor sapientis quærit doctrinam,
The heart of the wise seeks doctrine.
et os stultorum pascitur imperitia.
And the mouth of the foolish feeds on ignorance.
Omnes dies pauperis, mali;
All the days of the poor are evil.
secura mens quasi juge convivium.
A secure mind is like a continual feast.
Melius est parum cum timore Domini,
Better is a little with the fear of the Lord,
quam thesauri magni et insatiabiles.
than great treasures and dissatisfaction.
Melius est vocari ad olera cum caritate,
It is better to be called to vegetables with charity,
quam ad vitulum saginatum cum odio.
than to a fatted calf with hatred.
Vir iracundus provocat rixas;
A short-tempered man provokes conflicts.
qui patiens est mitigat suscitatas.
Whoever is patient tempers those who are stirred up.
Iter pigrorum quasi sepes spinarum;
The way of the slothful is like a hedge of thorns.
via justorum absque offendiculo.
The way of the just is without offense.
Filius sapiens lætificat patrem,
A wise son gladdens the father.
et stultus homo despicit matrem suam.
But the foolish man despises his mother.
Stultitia gaudium stulto,
Folly is gladness to the foolish.
et vir prudens dirigit gressus suos.
And the prudent man sets his own steps in order.
Dissipantur cogitationes ubi non est consilium;
Intentions dissipate where there is no counsel.
ubi vero sunt plures consiliarii,
Yet truly,
confirmantur.
they are confirmed where there are many counselors.
Lætatur homo in sententia oris sui,
A man rejoices in the verdict of his own mouth.
et sermo opportunus est optimus.
And a word at the right time is best.
Semita vitæ super eruditum,
The path of life is for the wise above,
ut declinet de inferno novissimo.
so that he may turn away from the end of Hell.
Domum superborum demolietur Dominus,
The Lord will demolish the house of the arrogant.
et firmos faciet terminos viduæ.
And He will make firm the borders of the widow.
Abominatio Domini cogitationes malæ,
Evil intentions are an abomination to the Lord.
et purus sermo pulcherrimus firmabitur ab eo.
And pure conversation, most beautiful, shall be confirmed by him.
Conturbat domum suam qui sectatur avaritiam;
Whoever pursues avarice disturbs his own house.
qui autem odit munera,
But whoever hates bribes shall live.
vivet.
Through mercy and faith,
Per misericordiam
sins are purged.
et fidem purgantur peccata:
But through the fear of the Lord,
per timorem autem Domini declinat omnis a malo.
each one turns aside from evil.
Mens justi meditatur obedientiam;
The mind of the just meditates on obedience.
os impiorum redundat malis.
The mouth of the impious overflows with evils.
Longe est Dominus ab impiis,
The Lord is distant from the impious.
et orationes justorum exaudiet.
And he will heed the prayers of the just.
Lux oculorum lætificat animam;
The light of the eyes rejoices the soul.
fama bona impinguat ossa.
A good reputation fattens the bones.
Auris quæ audit increpationes vitæ in medio sapientium commorabitur.
The ear that listens to the reproofs of life shall abide in the midst of the wise.
Qui abjicit disciplinam despicit animam suam;
Whoever rejects discipline despises his own soul.
qui autem acquiescit increpationibus possessor est cordis.
But whoever agrees to correction is a possessor of the heart.
Timor Domini disciplina sapientiæ,
The fear of the Lord is the discipline of wisdom.
et gloriam præcedit humilitas.
And humility precedes glory.
